paper_metadata.title: Effects of Nb addition on microstructure and mechanical properties of TiNiNb alloys fabricated by elemental powder sintering

evidence.quote: Porous TiNi binary and TiNiNb ternary alloys of four compositions (Ti50Ni47.5Nb2.5, Ti50Ni45Nb5, Ti50Ni42.5Nb7.5, and Ti50Ni40Nb10) were fabricated by the elemental powder sintering process.
Porous TiNi binary and TiNiNb ternary alloys of four compositions (Ti50Ni47.5Nb2.5, Ti50Ni45Nb5, Ti50Ni42.5Nb7.5, and Ti50Ni40Nb10) were fabricated by the elemental powder sintering process.
These elemental powders were blended for 4h in a roller mixer to produce powder mixtures with different nominal compositions of Ti50Ni50-xNbx (x=0, 2.5, 5, 7.5 and 10, at.%).

The powder mixtures were compacted under 300MPa pressure, and then the powder compacts were sintered at 1050 ℃ for 4 h in high vacuum ( ≤2.0×10-2 Pa) with a heat rate of 5 ℃/min to assure sufficient sintering.

When the Nb content is just 2.5 %, as a small amount of Nb destroyed the stable state of TiNi matrix, both tensile strength and elastic modulus are lower than those of TiNi binary alloy.
Whereas, with Nb contents increasing from 2.5 % to 10 %, the tensile strength and elastic modulus are improved from 131.21 MPa to 281.81 MPa and from 2.02 GPa to 3.29 GPa, respectively.

This can be explained as solid solution strengthening by the addition of Nb. As a strengthening element, the dissolving of Nb in TiNi matrix or Ti-rich zone causes lattice distortion. Thereby the dislocation glide becomes more difficult.
Large amount of Nb-rich particles embedded in matrix also plays a role through precipitation strengthening for the strength increment.
